question.problem: A computer program is designed so that it can randomly generate a real number between $0$ and $10,$ inclusive. What is the probability that the number generated is between $3$ and $7?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the number generated by the program. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U[0,10],$ and we wish to compute $P(3<X<7).$

In general, if $X∼U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a}, & a\le x\le b \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

So, for our random variable $X∼U[0,10],$ we have the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}, & 0\le x\le 10 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3<X<7) & ={\int }_{3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{7}\frac{1}{10}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{x}{10}|}_{3}^{7} \\  & =\frac{7}{10}-\frac{3}{10} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
